title.narrative: Core support to EPF Georgia phase III

description.narrative:
Eurasia Partnership Foundation (EPF) Georgien har ansökt om kärnstöd och insatsen heter "Core support to Eurasia Partnership Foundation Georgia 2014-2019". Sida har gett stöd till EPF i två tidigare "faser" sedan 2008.
Det övergripande målet för stödet till EPF i Georgien är att skapa förutsättningar för ökat deltagande i det civila samhället samt att öka medborgarnas inflytande över samhällsutvecklingen. EPF har stor räckvidd och når ut till gräsrotsorgansationer samt aktivister genom bidrag till partnerorganisationer och kapacitetsutveckling. EPF implementerar dessutom egna projekt som bidrar till att uppfylla organisationens mål. EPF:s projekt och bidrag handlar om EU-integrationen, att unga människor blir förändringsaktörer i sina lokala samhällen, att främja socialt företagande och att öka civilsamhällets deltagande i beslutsfattande. En del av stödet planeras fortsatt att gå till den s.k. "open-door" mekanismen där EPF löpande stödjer initiativ av pilotkaraktär som kan replikeras i andra kontexter. Speciellt fokus vid denna projektfas planeras ligga vid stöd till organisationer på landsbygden. Utvalda organisationer får stöd tillsammans med organisationsutvecklingsstöd.
Insatsens budget är 38,1 MSEK. EPF:s övriga givare ger projektstöd och är bland annat USAID, EU UNDP/COBERM.
Eurasia Partnership Foundation (EPF) Georgia has applied for support "Core Support for Partnership Foundation (EPF) Georgia 2014-2019". Sida has supported EPF in two phases since 2008.
The overarching goal for the support to EPF is to empower people to effect change for social justice and economic prosperity through hands-on programs, helping them to improve their communities and their own lives. EPF is reaching out to grassroot organizations, particularly in the regions, by providing grants and by implementing projects. It focuses on creating opportunities for civic participation in public policy making, promoting social enterprises, EU integration and engaging youth. A part of the project is planned to continue to go to the so called "open-door" mechanism, where EPF supports pilot projects that foster civic engagement and projects that have the potential to be replicated. A special focus will lay with supporting organizations in the regions. Selected organizations will receive institutional development and/or core support.
The intervention's total budget is 38,1 million SEK. Other donors to EPF include UNDP/COBERM and EU.

The overarching goal for the intervention and the core support to EPF Georgia is to create opportunities for civic engagement thereby increasing citizens' influence on the society's development. EPF reaches out to grassroot organizations, particularly in the regions, by providing grants and by implementing projects.It focuses on civic participation, engaging youth, social enterprising and EU-integration

Europe Foundations (EPF) mission is to empower people to effect change for social justice and economic prosperity through hands-on programs, helping them to improve their communities and their own lives.
To serve its mission the Europe Foundation defined the following outcomes:
Outcome: Enhanced civil society influence on public decision making process
Outcome: Civil society is engaged in and contributes to participatory decision making to achieve convergence to European standards and practices
Outcome: Enhanced female and male youth volunteerism and civic engagement to address target community needs
Outcome: Financial sustainability of CSOs is improved to contribute to enhanced and inclusive governance through enterprising non-profits in Georgia.
Relevant logframe was developed by the Foundation that included bridging outcomes.

Europe Foundations (EPF) mission is to empower people to effect change for social justice and economic prosperity through hands-on programs, helping them to improve their communities and their own lives. To achieve its mission, the Foundation strives (a) to strengthen the capacity of individuals and institutions, empowering them to address pressing issues and (b) to mobilize relevant stakeholders in issue-based dialogue, through raising public awareness and creating various coalitions, platforms or working groups, so as to effect positive change.
Thus Europe Foundation defined outcomes it planned to achieve during the project lifetime. Below are those outcomes and some achievements over the years 2014 - 2021.
Outcome: Enhanced civil society influence on public decision making process
In 2014-2021 participatory civic monitoring and advocacy actions undertaken by Europe Foundation grantees and partners resulted in 58 (instead of planned 36) tangible positive changes for Georgian citizens. These included successes in promoting inclusive education programming for children with disabilities, encouragement of needs-based budgeting, most notably for people with disabilities and their families, improved water supply systems and city infrastructure, institutionalized mechanisms for participatory decision making in several municipalities, and increased access to publicly held information.
Outcome: Civil society is engaged in and contributes to participatory decision making to achieve convergence to European standards and practices
EPF succeeded in achieving its projected outcome of increasing civil society participation in and influence over Georgias integration into the European Union. EPF reached all of its projected targets and, in many cases, the achievements were significantly higher than anticipated in 2013, when the 2014-2021 strategy was being prepared. By the end of the reporting period, 136 advocacy initiatives were implemented by or with participation of the Foundations grantees, partners, and beneficiaries and Georgia saw 85 cases of improved legislation and practice (mostly in Sanitary and Phyto Sanitary area), which were identified by CSOs and adopted by the GoG.
Outcome: Enhanced female and male youth volunteerism and civic engagement to address target community needs
To achieve the desired outcome of enhanced youth volunteerism and civic engagement, Europe Foundation has been employing a well-tested Youth Bank (YB) methodology, which was developed in Northern Ireland and then modified by the Foundation for Georgian context and needs. The YB model is founded on the premise that involving young people in projects they design and manage is the most potent way to develop civic participation among youth. During the reporting period, Europe Foundation recruited 967 youth (605 female), as members of YB Committees, who were then empowered through training and resources to find, fund, and oversee 660 small youth-led initiatives designed to address the issues faced by their respective communities. Through these initiatives, the program mobilized 10,445 (5,467 female) volunteers and directly benefited 46,068 (24,638 female) community members.
More specifically, the program covered 36 communities from 10 regions across Georgia. To support youth and equip them with the skills necessary to engage in community grantmaking, Europe Foundation organized 79 capacity building initiatives on topics ranging from community leadership and intercultural communications to media literacy, storytelling, food safety, water, hygiene, and sanitation, environmental protection, entrepreneurship, etc. The Foundations efforts to bolster youth civic participation also translated into 561 community initiatives implemented by the young volunteers outside the provided support.
Outcome: Financial sustainability of CSOs is improved to contribute to enhanced and inclusive governance through enterprising non-profits in Georgia.
Europe Foundation targeting the outcome created Social Enterprise Development Program aimed at putting the concept of social enterprise on a policy agenda so that it was increasingly utilized as a way of attaining long-term CSO sustainability to address the needs of their vulnerable constituencies. To this end, Europe Foundation promoted the concept of social enterprise and, as a result, fostered more engagement of public authorities and the businesses community in the efforts to support social enterprise development. In 2017, the concept was acknowledged by the GoG in a policy document and since then the work is under way to foster more enabling environment for social entrepreneurship in Georgia.
